Article Title: Asian Games Medal Tally: India win 8 medals but remain outside top 10 as gold continues to elude
Article Text:
Yashvir Singh, Rohit Yadav, and Esha Singh

Eight medals, but no gold for India

Shooting and kurash add to India's tally

Asian Games Medal Tally after Day 9

Rank Nation Gold Silver Bronze Total 1 China 132 53 45 230 2 Japan 41 68 63 172 3 South Korea 21 26 43 90 4 Uzbekistan 12 17 13 42 5 Kazakhstan 9 13 23 45 6 Thailand 9 8 13 30 7 Bahrain 9 2 3 14 8 Iran 8 15 9 32 9 North Korea 7 5 5 17 10 Malaysia 6 3 9 18 11 Hong Kong 5 12 17 34 12 INDIA 4 20 21 45

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. China led with 132 golds, followed by japan with 41, south korea with 21 and uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.

Article Title: Brij Bhushan acquittal challenged over ‘stereotypical assumptions’ about sexual assault victims
Article Text:
Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Rouse Avenue court has issued notice to former Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) chief Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh and others on an appeal challenging his acquittal in a sexual harassment case involving women wrestlers.Special Judge Dig Vinay Singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on October 9. The court also directed that the original affidavit and orders containing the names of the victims be placed in a sealed envelope. It further directed the appellant to file a copy of the petition with the victims’ names redacted.The appeal challenges the August 3 order of the Rouse Avenue court, Brij Bhushan and Vinod Tomar in the case. The wrestlers have contended that the acquittal order is unsustainable in law and is based on a “manifestly erroneous and selective appreciation of the evidence on record”.The appeal has contended that the impugned order proceeds on conjectures and surmises, fails to apply binding and well-settled principles of law, and, in material part, rests its reasoning on “archaic and stereotypical assumptions” about the “expected” behaviour of victims of sexual assault and harassment, rather than on a fair, evidence-based assessment after taking into account the circumstances of the victims.The case stems from an FIR filed by Delhi Police following a complaint by a woman wrestler during Singh’s tenure as WFI chief. The police had invoked Sections 354, 354-D, 354-A, 506(1) and 109 of the Indian Penal Code.Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar had acquitted Singh and Tomar after a trial that was conducted in a closed courtroom. The two were tried in connection with allegations of sexual harassment of women wrestlers in India and abroad.Delhi Police had filed a 1,500-page charge sheet against Singh and Tomar on June 15, 2023, following its investigation into the allegations.The women wrestlers had earlier staged a protest at Jantar Mantar, following which the FIR was registered by Delhi Police based on the complaint.Advocate Rajiv Mohan, assisted by Rehan Khan and Rishabh Bhati, represented Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh, while senior advocate Rebecca John appeared for the victims and complainants.
Article Summary: Wrestlers challenge acquittal, cite ‘stereotypical assumptions’ special judge dig vinay singh sought a response to the appeal and listed the matter for hearing on october 9. The appeal challenges the august 3 order of the rouse avenue court, brij bhushan and vinod tomar in the case.

Article Title: Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski FOX broadcast controversy enters a major phase after Bills veteran Micah Hyde revives old Patriots rivalry after Buffalo appearance
Article Text:
Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski FOX broadcast controversy enters a major phase after Bills veteran Micah Hyde remark(Image via Getty Images)

Bills veteran Micah Hyde opens up on Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski’s FOX role

Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots history still fuels Bills rivalry

Tom Brady and Rob Gronkowski’s FOX broadcast appearance during the Buffalo Bills’ Week 3 matchup with the Los Angeles Chargers brought back memories of one of the NFL’s biggest rivalries. Former Bills safety Micah Hyde made his feelings clear about seeing the two former New England Patriots stars around Buffalo’s game.Hyde’s comments quickly grabbed attention because his frustration came from years of battles against the Patriots. Brady and Gronkowski spent much of their careers creating difficult moments for Buffalo, and their return to the Bills’ stadium reminded fans of that history.During the Buffalo Plus podcast, Hyde explained why he did not enjoy seeing Brady and Gronkowski involved in the broadcast of the Bills’ Week 3 game on September 21, 2026.“Tom Brady calling Bills games, I’m not a fan of. And Gronk on the sideline talking to Josh before, like, not a fan of that,” Hyde said on the podcast.Hyde also reacted to Gronkowski’s sideline interaction with Bills quarterback Josh Allen before the game and questioned why former Patriots players were covering a Buffalo matchup.The former Bills safety added that he did not want to see Brady at Highmark Stadium because of the history between the quarterback and Buffalo.“Get out of here. No one, I don’t wanna see you on TV talking, being at the Bills stadium and stuff,” Hyde said during the podcast. “You know, you hate the Bills. And the Bills hate you.”The comments reflected the old AFC East rivalry between Buffalo and New England, especially during Brady’s 20-year run with the Patriots.Brady dominated the Bills during his Patriots career. The seven-time Super Bowl champion finished his regular-season matchups against Buffalo with a 33-3 record.Gronkowski also played a major role in New England’s success against the Bills. The tight end faced Buffalo 16 times and recorded 74 receptions for 1,132 yards and 12 touchdowns in those games.Hyde’s relationship with the Patriots rivalry goes beyond Brady and Gronkowski’s statistics. He spent seven seasons with Buffalo after joining the team in 2017 and became a key part of the defense alongside Jordan Poyer.During his Bills career, Hyde recorded 417 tackles and 16 interceptions. He earned two second-team All-Pro selections and one Pro Bowl appearance before retiring after the 2024 season.His frustration with New England also came from moments during his playing days. After a 2019 game against the Patriots where Josh Allen suffered a hit, Hyde criticized the officiating and referenced how players would have been treated if a similar play involved Brady.Meanwhile, Brady added another reminder of his history with Buffalo while calling the September 2026 game. During the broadcast, he joked about his success against the Bills, mentioning his record at the old Highmark Stadium.Despite the attention around the FOX broadcast team, Buffalo finished the night with the final say. The Bills defeated the Chargers 24-16 after overcoming a 10-0 deficit. Josh Allen threw for 204 yards and rushed for two touchdowns, while James Cook added 154 rushing yards and a score.The rivalry between Brady’s Patriots era and Buffalo’s current generation continues to create headlines, even years after those battles ended on the field.
Article Summary: Former bills safety micah hyde made his feelings clear about seeing the two former new england patriots stars around buffalo’s game. Brady and gronkowski spent much of their careers creating difficult moments for buffalo, and their return to the bills’ stadium reminded fans of that history.

Article Title: Aaron Rodgers says there is "zero debate" about retiring, yet his final Thursday night game feels like unfinished business
Article Text:
Aaron Rodgers’ Steelers face Browns in his final Thursday night game as Pittsburgh tries to erase a 46-year nightmare (Image via Getty Images)

Is Aaron Rodgers really retiring after the 2026 season?

Can the Steelers beat the Browns on a short week?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Aaron Rodgers will play the last scheduled Thursday night game of his career when the Pittsburgh Steelers visit the Cleveland Browns at 8:15 p.m. ET on Amazon Prime. He sits one win short of tying Tom Brady's record of 14 Thursday wins by a quarterback. Both teams are 2-1. The Steelers beat Cincinnati 30-27 last week, and the Browns edged Carolina 21-18. Pittsburgh also arrives with an 0-9 mark in Thursday road games against AFC North opponents. Rodgers, 42, plans to retire after this 22nd season, so Cleveland is his final shot at matching Brady's number.Everything he has said points to yes. Rodgers signed a one-year deal with Pittsburgh in May after more than four months of deliberating. Asked whether this would be his last season, he told reporters, “Yes, this is it.” When he returned to training camp on July 28, a reporter asked if he was weighing another year after this one. His answer was short. “No. Zero debate.”That certainty changes how Thursday reads. Rodgers turns 43 in December, and this is his last scheduled Thursday game. Brady's mark is 14, so a win ties it and nothing more. There is no later date to push past him.Rodgers has 46 touchdowns and seven interceptions on Thursdays. Against Cleveland, he has thrown 11 touchdowns without an interception in five games.He does not sound sentimental about the night itself. “I just suck it up for those three hours and then know you get a reward on the back end. I think it’s part of the game now because of the money that’s in it. I think I’m just excited about the weekend,” Rodgers said. If the Brady record matters to him, he is keeping it quiet.History says be careful. Pittsburgh has lost all nine Thursday road games against AFC North teams, and four of those came against Cleveland. The Browns won 24-19 in a snowstorm two years ago. The 2019 meeting is remembered for Myles Garrett ripping off Mason Rudolph's helmet and hitting him with it. Cleveland has also won seven straight Thursday games, tied for the fourth-longest streak in NFL history.Defensive tackle Cam Heyward does not see the short week as a one-sided problem. “But the great thing about it is they got to deal with the same problems we are. So it’s an even playing field,” he said.The Steelers have roster questions, though. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. went to Dallas late Wednesday for two draft picks after a contract impasse, and Jalen Ramsey is questionable with a broken wrist. Jaylen Warren should carry the load again after a career-high 176 total yards against Cincinnati, since Rico Dowdle is out with a toe injury.The line play may decide it. Browns tackles have allowed a 13.5% pressure rate, second highest in the league, and Tytus Howard's 17 pressures are tied for the most by a right tackle. TJ Watt has 17.5 sacks in 15 games against Cleveland. Deshaun Watson has lost all three starts against Pittsburgh and been sacked 18 times. Mike McCarthy is 11-5 on Thursday nights, and the Steelers are 2.5-point favorites.
Article Summary: Aaron rodgers will play the last scheduled thursday night game of his career when the pittsburgh steelers visit the cleveland browns at 8:15 p.m. Et on amazon prime. He sits one win short of tying tom brady's record of 14 thursday wins by a quarterback. Rodgers, 42, plans to retire after this 22nd season, so cleveland is his final shot at matching brady's number.

Article Title: “My fiancé finds me crying in bed”: Aryna Sabalenka opens up on losing her father and ex boyfriend amid China Open return
Article Text:

Aryna Sabalenka gears up for China Open

Aryna Sabalenka could be one of the greatest athletes that the world has ever seen but she has constantly battled against a lot of negative events in her life. While losing her father in 2019 was one of the tragedies in her life, Aryna Sabalenka also found it difficult to deal with when her ex boyfriend, former NHL player Konstantin Koltsov, committed suicide in 2024.In an interview with Vogue, Aryna Sabalenka reflected on being approached by cops at her practice courts as she said, “I was fighting with the cop — like, I couldn’t accept it…”In another interview with TIME, the 28 year old tennis star added, “Tennis really saved me from depression…I was just trying to focus on training, just so I spend less time with myself in my thoughts. I would cry in practice a lot. It was a very tough moment in my life.”The tennis star continued, “I don’t know if there’s any cliché about how you’re supposed to grieve,” she said. “I feel like in this situation, there is no right and wrong. We all need different things. For me, going back to work is the only way. I’m 28, but sometimes I think I’ve had everything in life that you could imagine.”Aryna Sabalenka reflected on how losing her father at a pretty young age has constantly made her sad as she added, “Nowadays my fiancé will find me crying in bed in the evening because I’m watching Reels and there’s something about a father, or old times,” she shared.“The most sensitive videos for me are when I see people posting a family reaction to their kid athlete winning something, and I just imagine how my dad would react to me. ”But this was not the first time that she has spoken about it; in many of her previous interviews, the tennis star has reflected on the regrets she has had with her father’s as she even blamed paramedics for not being able to hospitalise him at the right time.Despite the immense grief that Aryna Sabalenka has carried for the last few years, she has remained strong and has worked pretty hard on her career.For now, her focus remains on the China Open as Aryna Sabalenka enters the WTA 1000 tournament in Beijing as the No. 2 seed. She received a first round bye and automatically advanced to the round of 64 because of her high seeding.Aryna Sabalenka is scheduled to play her opening match at the 2026 China Open against Mexico's Renata Zarazúa today, October 2, 2026, on the Diamond Court.

Article Title: Caitlin Clark’s latest WNBA punishment explained: Fever guard’s Brianna Turner clash adds drama to Game 3 showdown vs Aces
Article Text:
Caitlin Clark was hit with a technical foul. Image via: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

Caitlin Clark receives technical foul after shoving Brianna Turner

How close is Caitlin Clark to a WNBA playoff suspension?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Caitlin Clark picked up a technical foul in the opening minutes of a win-or-go-home Game 3, and the cause was a former teammate who showed up inside Indiana's huddle. Brianna Turner got one too. Nobody shot a free throw, but the call put her playoff run on thinner ice.It happened Thursday, Oct. 1, in Las Vegas, with 6:54 left in the first quarter and officials still reviewing a foul on A'ja Wilson. The Fever were up 12-6. Then came the shove, a theatrical stumble and a double whistle.Caitlin Clark's technical in Game 3 against the Las Vegas Aces grew out of a play that began with someone else. Fever forward Lexie Hull was whistled for fouling Wilson on a rebound attempt. Referees went to the monitor to decide whether the call should be upgraded.While they checked, Indiana's starters gathered on the floor. Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, Hull, Aliyah Boston and Makayla Timpson formed a quick huddle. Brianna Turner was standing nearby, and she drifted into the circle. The Fever guard did not appear to say a word. She walked straight up to Turner and pushed her out.Turner flung her arms up and staggered back, selling the contact for all it was worth.Turner played for Indiana in 2025, so the two know each other well. Whether Turner was hunting for information or just trying to break the group's focus is hard to say, though it looked like one or the other.After the review, officials gave both players a technical. Because the calls offset, neither team went to the line.The Fever guard had been here before. Her first technical of the postseason came Tuesday in Game 2, when Clark was called for an offensive foul after pushing Las Vegas guard Mai Yamamoto and appeared to wave off the official. It is unclear whether Clark said anything that earned the technical. Indiana trailed 29-20 at that point and then ripped off a 28-14 run.Closer than the Fever would like. Under WNBA rules, a player or coach is suspended for one game when the fourth technical of the postseason is called. Clark has two, so the Indiana guard sits halfway there. Each technical after that costs $1,500, and every two more adds another one-game ban.Counts reset when the regular season ends. Clark finished with seven, one short of the eighth that would have forced a suspension, so the playoffs began with a clean slate. The league can also review and rescind technicals, which means no total is final until the WNBA says so.Game 3 carried its own risk. With a technical already on the books, a second one in the same game would have meant an ejection for either player.The series had already been intense. Las Vegas won Game 1 at home, and Indiana forced this decider with a win at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Tuesday. Wilson drew a controversial conduct technical in that game after confronting a fan under the baseline.
Article Summary: Caitlin clark was hit with a technical foul. Brianna turner got one too. Nobody shot a free throw, but the call put her playoff run on thinner ice. Each technical after that costs $1,500, and every two more adds another one-game ban.

Article Title: Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James? Spurs star drops candid reaction after NBA veteran’s eyebrow-raising Polymarket deal
Article Text:
Victor Wembanyama and LeBron James. Image via: Daniel Dunn-Imagn Images

Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James?

How other NBA stars have taken betting money

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Victor Wembanyama has recently gave his honest reaction to the sports betting debate. At Spurs training camp on Thursday, a reporter asked whether the San Antonio center would ever promote a gambling company. "Absolutely not," he replied instantly. He further explained why he is dead set on staying out of it.The reigning Defensive Player of the Year spoke just weeks after LeBron James signed a Polymarket partnership expected to pay him $15 million a year. Wembanyama never mentioned the 76ers star by name but he certainly appears to take aim at the NBA veteran.Victor Wembanyama was answering a general question about sports betting sponsorships, and he spoke about the practice rather than one player. Asked on Thursday, October 1, he called it "very sad to see some players promote it." Then he added a line with a little edge, everybody does what they want, but without him.For those who have been aware of LeBron James's Polymarket deal, it certainly looks like an apparent slam at James, and the 76ers star is the obvious reference point. The 41-year-old announced a multi-year Polymarket partnership a few weeks ago, and he is expected to earn $15 million a year from it.James also signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Philadelphia this summer. One year of Polymarket money is worth more than that entire deal.Wembanyama explained the reasoning without pointing at anyone. "Obviously, we earn millions and millions," he said, before moving the conversation to influence. A player's biggest strength, according to the Spurs big man, is the ability to inspire, and that can go in a good direction or a bad one. "I want to inspire in a good way."Wembanyama has turned down endorsement offers before when the values behind them did not match. He does sign deals, though. A new Nike agreement includes a signature sneaker line.Wembanyama is stepping away from a crowded field. Giannis Antetokounmpo took an equity stake in Kalshi in February, and the Miami Heat star handles promotional work for the prediction market too. Kevin Durant has turned up regularly in FanDuel commercials, and his entertainment network, Boardroom, is partnered with the company. James had a similar arrangement with DraftKings before the Polymarket deal.Betting sponsorships have gone mainstream as the major leagues embrace gambling, and several NBA names now work with betting companies or prediction markets. More current and retired athletes could follow as the industry keeps growing. Wembanyama has said he will never be one of them.
Article Summary: Victor wembanyama says he will never promote a sports betting company. The san antonio spurs center made the comments at spurs training camp. Lebron james recently announced a multi-year polymarket partnership. James is expected to earn $15 million a year from the deal.

Article Title: 20 golds lost, just one individual title won: India’s Asian Games slide offers a stark reality check
Article Text:
Manu Bhaker and Satwik-Chirag (Agency Image)

A different gold-medal profile

Two more chances

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

With the Asian Games entering the final stretch, India’s declining gold medal numbers tell an uncomfortable story and offer a sharp reality check. Of the 28 golds India won in Hangzhou three years ago, 20 have already slipped away in Aichi-Nagoya, across shooting, athletics, archery, badminton, equestrian, squash and tennis. The sharpest contrast comes in individual events. In Hangzhou, India won nine individual gold medals across shooting, athletics and archery. None of those have been defended and, in some events, India was not even able to make the final rounds in the ongoing edition.In 2023, India produced a historic 106-medal haul: 28 gold, 38 silver and 40 bronze. Shooting alone delivered seven golds and athletics six, while archery completed a clean sweep of all five compound golds.Three years later, India has lost all seven shooting golds it won in Hangzhou and all six in athletics. In archery, the three team titles have survived, but neither of the individual ones. In squash, the country has lost both its titles from 2023 in the men’s team event and mixed doubles. The Hangzhou golds in badminton men’s doubles, team dressage and tennis mixed doubles have also not been retained.As of Thursday, India has won 10 gold medals at Aichi-Nagoya, with men’s hockey and cricket still carrying title-defence possibilities.India’s overall medal tally has crossed 60 and the country is eighth overall, but it is staring at a far lower haul than at Hangzhou. For perspective, China has so far won 154 gold medals and 288 medals overall.Particularly worrying is the disappearance of gold medals that India had already established as its continental benchmark.India’s campaign in Aichi-Nagoya has produced its share of memorable performances, new champions and hard-earned podium finishes. But with just two days left for the continental event to wind up, the larger picture is difficult to ignore: India has not been able to build on the gold-medal gains of Hangzhou.The six successful defences have come in men’s and women’s kabaddi, all three compound archery team events and women’s cricket. In Aichi-Nagoya, among the 10 gold medals won by India so far, only one has come in an individual event: Neeru Dhanda’s historic women’s trap triumph.The rest have come through team, relay or mixed formats. That is a substantial shift in the profile of India’s gold-medal success.India is not finished. The men’s hockey team has reached the gold-medal match after narrowly beating Pakistan 4-3 in the semifinal. The men’s cricket team has also reached the final, where it will face Pakistan after beating Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the semifinal.If India wins these two, the Hangzhou-to-Aichi-Nagoya comparison will improve from six successful defences to eight. But even a two-from-two finish would leave the basic statistic untouched: 20 of the Hangzhou golds would still have been lost.That is the number that should concern Indian sport administrators.It is not merely a case of one or two champions falling short. It points to a much broader problem of converting a successful Asian Games cycle into sustained dominance.The athletes who have won medals in Japan deserve full credit. The question is different: what happened between a record 28-gold campaign in Hangzhou and a Games in which the majority of those titles have not been retained?The answer cannot be found merely in the final medal table.Hangzhou demonstrated that India could win 28 golds. Aichi-Nagoya is demonstrating how difficult it is to make those gains sustainable.From 28 golds to 10: India’s Asian Games slide offers a stark reality check
Article Summary: Of the 28 golds india won in hangzhou three years ago, 20 have already slipped away in aichi-nagoya. The sharpest contrast comes in individual events. In hangzhou, india won nine individual gold medals across shooting, athletics and archery. None of those have been defended.

Article Title: ‘If India won a medal, we owe it to her’: Captain Swayams Mishra on Savitha Shri’s Chess Olympiad heroics | Exclusive
Article Text:
The challenges for Swayams started even before the tournament. Getting the team to that stage was a project in itself, with busy, overlapping schedules making it difficult for the players to train together in person.

The coffee, the bananas, and the helplessness of watching

Build-up: Virtual camps, and logistics that nearly derailed things again

The Vaishali decision

Board-by-board analysis from the captain

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you believe that the decision to not play Vaishali in some matches was justified? Yes, it was the right decision. No, she should have played more. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Bronze, and what the team takes from it

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Across the open and women's sections at the Chess Olympiad, only one player won an individual gold medal for India at the 2026 Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. That was Chennai's 19-year-old Savitha Shri Baskar. Savitha was often the one India could rely on when the team was staring at heartbreak. With her games routinely going down to the wire, she was kept fuelled, game after game, by someone making sure she never had to think about anything other than the board during India's bronze-clinching campaign."If we wanted something, he was always there, giving us everything, like water, bananas, and for me, he was bringing endless coffees because I played till the last moment, making sure that I ate properly and got energy," Savitha recalled, before labelling Swayams Mishra as the "best captain ever".For Mishra, it was new territory in a role he'd long been adjacent to."I've been part of the women's team since 2022, but this was the first time I was captaining completely. In 2024, I had captained for a couple of games, but this was a completely new experience," he told TimesofIndia.com during an exclusive interaction."This time, I have to be there in the tournament hall with the players, especially in the critical games, so the emotions are completely different compared to when you are outside.That was slightly different, and not easy."The job, according to Mishra, was less about tactics and more about manoeuvres of a different kind."It was hectic and exhausting, because as a captain you try to follow all the games going on, not just one player's. At the same time, sometimes you see a player making a mistake; you want to do something, but you cannot; you just have to wait for it to unfold naturally," he admitted. What he could control, though, he controlled."What I tried to do is look at what the players needed. If there's a longer game, they needed some energy or something to eat, so I made sure they had it available instead of spending time getting it themselves around the third or fourth hour."Viewers watching the live broadcast of the games got to witness the results of that instinct in real time, with water bottles, bananas, and coffee cups appearing at just the right moments.The challenges for Swayams started even before the tournament. Getting the team to that stage was a project in itself, with busy, overlapping schedules making it difficult for the players to train together in person.With the help of the All India Chess Federation (AICF), the team turned to virtual camps in the run-up to the Olympiad."It all started with the camps, like organising the camp online, where we found that most of the players' schedules were very tight, so we held an online camp because players were not able to find a common timing to able to meet up with their busy schedules," Mishra revealed.The challenges followed the team in Samarkand, where India, like several other nations, faced accommodation and food issues."On the first day, with the issues with the stay, AICF stepped up, and the president Nitin Narang and the HOD Abhijit Kunte ensured that the players got the rooms first," he said. "President Narang was also present, and he went out of his way to help us in most of the things."Food then became another issue, with Mishra recalling that “when food was not very ideal, the options were not great, AICF made sure that food is Indian food people get so that they don't lack energy and they don't go like let's say their routine and other things are not disturbed as well.”The team bronze did not come easy, without its share of difficult calls. One of the toughest was deciding which four players from the five-member squad would take the board each round."For me, it was not easy choosing whom to play, because it was always a tricky call, with Savitha and Vantika performing very well on the last boards, and Vaishali also having good chances; we wanted her to play. It's a very hard call when one of your top players ends up not being in form, and the others are performing very well. Vaishali tried, gave her best, but it just wasn't meant to be," the captain, who then decided to keep the Women's World Championship challenger on the board for only six out of the eleven games, sighed.With Vaishali, who had just one win in the entire Olympiad and finished with a score of 2.5/6, due to challenge for the Women's World Championship title next year, Mishra also addressed whether this stretch of poor form carried any psychological weight into that bigger picture."We had a discussion, and she was not thinking at all about the World Championship. She wanted to just focus and give her best for India in this Olympiad, but it wasn't working out. I think she's strong enough, a professional player who should be able to get back much stronger and prove herself as a world champion as well. I wish she wins the World Championship.""Humpy on board one, I think, this would be her best Olympiad. India hadn't won a medal on board one for quite some time, and her winning one (a bronze with a score of 7/10), undefeated, against strong opposition, was very good. We were never on the back foot on board one," captain Mishra explained.Board two, however, told a different story."Vaishali started off decently. She had some tough opponents who didn't make mistakes and played precisely against her. Against Poland, that's where things changed — she had a better position, in fact, and wanted to win. There were a couple of chances to simplify into a draw, but she wanted to win, and in that process ended up making mistakes and losing," the coach added."Then she had another critical game against Kazakhstan, where she again had chances to equalise but wanted to win it for the team. A draw there would have given us 2-2, because Savitha's board wasn't clear yet. So she tried, and it backfired. You can say she was always there for the team, even if her performance wasn't great."By contrast, individual silver medalist Divya Deshmukh, scoring 6.5/10, emerged as one of the pillars."She took a lot of blacks, seven out of ten games, and was always ready whenever the team needed her. She had a consistent performance and gave us a couple of fast wins that put pressure on the other opponents."It came after a rough patch as Mishra continued, "She started completely out of form; Cairns Cup wasn't as per expectations, GCL wasn't great. But from there, she came back very strongly and was always reliable. She lost the last round, but she'd done her job by then."Vantika Agrawal, on board four for most of the tournament before Savitha's emergence, drew measured praise."She was consistent. There was one game, against China, that was very close, where she was close to a draw and missed something under pressure. Otherwise, she did her job, whatever was assigned to her, and gave us points on the last board," he added.And then Savitha. Mishra didn't hold back on addressing the scrutiny that had followed her selection."There were a lot of people who questioned her spot, journalists saying there are players higher than her, and so on. But according to the selection, she was qualified, and she'd won the Asian continental a couple of months ago. She'd also played the World Women's Team Championship, so I knew her as a team player always."Whenever we gave her the opportunity, she delivered. From round seven onwards, her form dropped slightly compared to the initial rounds as she was making some errors; the quality wasn't quite what she'd have expected. But she always compensated in the last hour, changing the result of the match completely. If India won a medal, we owe it to her."Asked whether anyone inside the camp was satisfied with bronze, Mishra didn't pretend otherwise."We are not satisfied. The colour of the medal would have been different, and we would have been much happier. But even in your not-so-good times, if you're able to get a medal, that shows how strong the team is. We expect to come back even stronger next year and win gold."I know people might be disappointed; the fans might be disappointed; we're equally disappointed. But everyone tried their best. The margins were very close."The tournament's bigger lesson, for him, had less to do with India specifically than with the state of women's chess as a whole."We did not underestimate anyone, but there were a lot of teams creating upsets. Mongolia, whom we played in round four, and Greece in round three, both ended up causing upsets elsewhere. Against the silver-winning Kazakh team, Mongolia were winning too, before it finished 2-2. In the last few Olympiads it was smooth sailing for the top seeds.This year, weaker teams were able to strike. That means chess is growing in general, especially women's chess. "ALSO READ: 'Unrealistic to win gold every single time': Captain Srinath Narayanan after India's silver at Chess Olympiad | Exclusive It's a tournament Mishra will remember as much for its margins as its medal, a campaign where India were, by his own description, "always on the wrong side of where we wanted to be", rescued more than once by a teenager fuelled on endless cups of coffee, and still, somehow, bronze rather than nothing at all.
Article Summary: India won bronze at the 2026 chess olympiad in samarkand, uzbekistan. Chennai's 19-year-old savitha shri baskar won an individual gold medal. Swayams mishra captained the team for the first time. Mishra says the job was hectic and exhausting. The team bronze did not come easy, without its share of difficult calls.

Article Title: 'Full respect' for India: Carlo Ancelotti's big message before Brazil clash
Article Text:
India's head coach Khalid Jamil, left, and Brazil's head coach Carlos Ancelotti (AP Photo)

Ancelotti: India game an opportunity, not a test

Building a new Brazil

Ancelotti wants Brazil to play with joy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti expects an entertaining contest against India on Saturday, insisting that his side have "full respect" for their opponents and viewing the game as an opportunity rather than a test for his players.The five-time Champions League-winning manager, who took charge of Brazil in May 2025 ahead of the 2026 World Cup, said he was pleased to be in India and keen to see his team showcase its quality.“I hope it will be an entertaining game. We’re happy to be here and to show our quality,” Ancelotti said.Brazil come into the game after playing two matches in Australia, drawing one 1-1 and winning the other 4-2. Their visit to India is another part of Ancelotti's preparations as he works to bring together a squad containing a mix of established players and new faces.With Brazil still finalising their combination, Ancelotti dismissed the idea that Saturday's match would be an examination for individual players.Asked whether the fixture represented a test for his squad, he said: “For the squad and all the players, it’s not a test or an opportunity to prove themselves. We are still defining the final squad for the match. It’s not a test, but an opportunity.”Ancelotti also declined to reveal his starting XI when asked directly.Asked to name his starting XI, Ancelotti simply replied: “No.”The Italian said Brazil had closely followed India's recent performance against Panama, in which the hosts played out a 1-1 draw.“We have respect for the quality of the Indian team. They played a good draw against Panama. We have full respect for our opponents,” he said.He also stressed that patience is part of his approach as a manager.“It’s part of my character. I’m usually patient in football, and as a manager, I think patience is an important quality,” he said.Ancelotti has been using this phase to assess a squad that combines experienced names with several new additions. Vinicius Jr and Marquinhos provide experience, while Arsenal duo Gabriel Magalhaes and Bruno Guimaraes have retained their places.There have been significant changes in goal, with Alisson, Ederson and Weverton, the trio used at the World Cup, left out. Corinthians' Hugo Souza has taken over as the first-choice goalkeeper, with Coritiba's Pedro Morisco and Cruzeiro's Otavio serving as his back-ups.The defensive unit has also been reshaped, with Arthur Dias, Jair, Matheuzinho and Mauro Junior included alongside established figures such as Marquinhos and Magalhaes.Ancelotti said bringing the group together had been a positive experience as Brazil prepare for the next stage of their development.“It’s a pleasure to work with all of the new members. Not only them, but the whole squad. It has been a great moment, bringing them together, creating synergy and feeling the energy in the squad,” he said.The manager also highlighted the differences between working at club level and with a national team, where preparation time is considerably shorter.“Training at clubs and training with a national team is very different. You have to select the right players. At a club, you have more time to do the right things. It is special to train the national team of Brazil,” he said.The matches in Australia and India are also part of that process.“All these games in Australia and India are good preparation and a good opportunity to show what we can do,” Ancelotti said.While rebuilding the squad, Ancelotti said there were certain characteristics he wanted to remain at the heart of Brazil's football.“Commitment, quality and happiness to play football. Quality is part of our culture. I would like the players to enjoy themselves, to play with happiness in every game. You want to play with joy,” he said.Brazil have not lifted the World Cup since their 2002 triumph in Japan and South Korea. Their latest campaign ended with a pre-quarterfinal defeat to Norway, and Ancelotti admitted the team had not competed at the level required.“It’s true that we were not able to compete enough in the World Cup. It was a difficult period for us. It is motivation for a new generation of players to be able to compete at the highest level in the coming years,” he said.Asked why Brazil have struggled to reproduce the success of the 2002 generation, Ancelotti pointed to the evolution of the game and the improvement of other teams.“It’s difficult. I can only answer for what happened in 2026. We had problems that we were not able to solve. Football has changed, and other teams have improved a lot,” he said.“In my personal opinion, the talent Brazil was able to show in 2002 was big talent. Football has changed. There is more teamwork now,” he added.
Article Summary: Carlo ancelotti expects an entertaining contest against india on saturday. The italian says his side have "full respect" for their opponents. Brazil are preparing for the 2026 world cup with a squad containing a mix of established players and new faces. Brazil have not lifted the world cup since their 2002 triumph in japan and south korea.

India’s medal-winning campaign at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 reached 72 medals on October 2 so far, with the contingent winning 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.India added six medals on Day 13, including gold medals for boxer Lovlina Borgohain and the women’s recurve archery team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod. Kumkum also won a silver alongside Dhiraj Bommadevara in the mixed recurve team event, while Dhiraj, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge secured silver in the men’s recurve team event.Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women’s dinghy sailing event, while India’s men’s quadrant team added another bronze in sepaktakraw. India are currently sixth in the medal standings with 12 gold, 25 silver and 35 bronze medals.India’s women’s cricket team won the country’s first gold medal of the Games after defeating Sri Lanka in the final. Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet then added India’s second gold by winning the 10m air pistol mixed team event. The pair topped qualification before finishing first in the final.India subsequently won both the men’s and women’s kabaddi titles, while Neeru Dhanda secured gold in the women’s trap event. She later teamed up with Kynan Chenai to win the mixed trap team gold.In athletics, Kiran Pahal, Poovamma Machettira, Prachi Choudhary and Vithya Ramraj won gold in the women’s 4x400m relay. India also dominated the compound archery events, winning gold in the men’s team, women’s team and mixed team eventsOn October 2, Lovlina Borgohain defeated China’s Bao Ziyi 5-0 in the women’s 75kg final to win gold.The victory came on her birthday and made Lovlina only the second Indian woman boxer after Mary Kom to win an Asian Games gold.The women’s recurve team of Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and Kumkum Mohod then created history by defeating South Korea 5-3 to win India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the event.India’s silver medal haul has come across shooting, athletics, weightlifting, wushu, squash, wrestling, sailing and archery. The shooting contingent has been one of India’s biggest contributors, with medals across air rifle, 50m rifle 3 positions, 25m pistol and trap events.Mirabai Chanu ended her long wait for an Asian Games medal by taking silver in the women’s 49kg weightlifting event, while Roshibina Devi won silver in women’s 60kg sanda. Gulveer Singh has also enjoyed a strong Games, winning silver in the men’s 10,000m and 1500m events.In squash, Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh won silver in the women’s and men’s singles events respectively. India added three silver medals on October 2. Kumkum Mohod and Dhiraj Bommadevara lost 3-5 to China in the mixed recurve final, while Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Yashdeep Bhoge lost to South Korea in the men’s recurve team final.India’s bronze medals have come from a wide range of disciplines, including shooting, athletics, squash, boxing, wrestling, archery, sailing, sepaktakraw, badminton, rowing, table tennis, kurash, soft tennis and mixed martial arts.Athletics has produced a large share of India’s bronze medals, with Parul Chaudhary, Gulveer Singh, Tejaswin Shankar, Vithya Ramraj, Pooja Singh, Rohit Yadav and others contributing to the tally. India’s squash contingent has also produced multiple medals, with Joshna Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar, Anahat Singh, Tanvi Khanna, Abhay Singh and Veer Chotrani contributing across the mixed doubles and team events.In boxing, Narender Berwal, Priya Ghanghas and Kapil Pokhariya won bronze, while Sunil Kumar secured bronze in Greco-Roman wrestling. On October 2, Nethra Kumanan won bronze in the women’s dinghy event, while India’s men’s sepaktakraw quadrant team also secured bronze after losing 0-2 to Japan in the semifinal.

India’s bronze medal winners at asian games 2026 are: suchika tariyal mixed martial arts. India won the bronze medal for the first time in the history of the asian games.

Article Title: A 500-year-old football was found in a queen’s bedroom; in 2026, scientists scanned it so the object could live digitally
Article Text:
The ball was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland | LEFT: Wikimedia Commons; RIGHT: instagram.@dr.futbal

The ball was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland | LEFT: Wikimedia Commons; RIGHT: instagram.@dr.futbal

The ball spent centuries out of sight

Stirling Castle in Scotland | Wikimedia Commons

From castle rafters to a World Cup

A leather football that dates to around 1540 has spent centuries behind the walls of Stirling Castle and was discovered during renovation work in the late 1970s. The ball was recognised by Guinness World Records as the world’s oldest football, and was found behind panelling in the Queen’s Chamber at Stirling Castle in Scotland. The chamber had been decorated in the 1540s, when Mary, Queen of Scots, was a child at the castle. The ball itself is dated to between 1540 and 1570, according to the Stirling Smith Art Gallery & Museum , which now holds it.The ball stopped at the University of Glasgow, where specialists began scanning it to produce a museum-quality digital twin, before travelling to the United States for the FIFA World Cup. The digital project uses a process called photogrammetry that combines photographs that are taken from different angles to build a detailed three-dimensional representation. University of Glasgow specialists Conor Fraser and Ben Morris captured the ball before it travelled to Miami for the Scotland-Brazil match on June 24. The university said the digital version will allow people to examine details such as its stitching and worn leather surface.The Stirling Smith describes the football as roughly the size of a small melon, and measured about 160 millimetres long, 150 millimetres wide and 140 millimetres high.It was made from thick leather panels that were stitched together and turned inside out, and inside was an inflated pig’s bladder, which provided the ball’s shape. The museum says that several repairs remain visible on its surface, which is evidence that the object was used rather than made simply for display.How it ended up behind the panelling is not known, with one possibility being that it was kicked into the roof space and became trapped there, while another is that someone deliberately put it there and forgot about it. The museum also notes the possibility that it was placed there for a symbolic purpose, although there is no evidence establishing which explanation is correct.The ball was found in a chamber that was associated with Mary, Queen of Scots, and historical records show that she took an interest in sport. But there is no evidence that she personally owned or played with this particular football, and Guinness World Records says that it is more likely that soldiers or staff at the castle used the ball for a form of handball.The football was eventually placed in the collection of the Stirling Smith Art Gallery & Museum, where it became one of the institution’s best-known objects. Guinness World Records lists it as the oldest football and dates its manufacture to the 1540–1570 period. The ball was scheduled to appear at the Coral Gables Museum in Florida from June 20 to 24 before being taken to the Scotland-Brazil World Cup match in Miami, and the University of Glasgow said it was the first time that the football had travelled to the United States.The university has been developing its “Wonder” platform through its Museums in the Metaverse programme, and used 3D models to let people examine cultural objects virtually. For a museum object that normally has to remain protected behind glass, the digital version changes how it can be viewed. A visitor does not have to travel to Stirling to see its surface at close range, and the model can be enlarged or examined from different angles without handling the original.The physical football remains at the Stirling Smith when it is not travelling, with its leather surface, old repairs and unusual construction still belonging to a fragile object that survived from the 16th century. The new scan just gives researchers and visitors another way to examine the same evidence.
Article Summary: The ball was found behind panelling in the queen’s chamber at stirling castle in scotland. The chamber had been decorated in the 1540s, when mary, queen of scots, was a child at the castle. The ball itself is dated to between 1540 and 1570, according to the stirling smith art gallery & museum.

Article Title: ‘I wanted to quit boxing’: Lovlina Borgohain fights through tough year to script historic Asian Games gold
Article Text:
Gold medallist India's Lovlina Borgohain (PTI Photo)

From Paris heartbreak to Asiad glory

‘I am feeling very good’

‘You are confident, you are the best’

NEW DELHI: A year after questioning her future in boxing, Lovlina Borgohain found the perfect answer on Friday, winning Asian Games gold on her 29th birthday.The 29-year-old had contemplated walking away from boxing after returning empty-handed from the Paris Olympics. Two years later, after enduring a difficult phase and questioning her future in the sport, Lovlina stood on top of the podium at the Asian Games — becoming only the second Indian woman boxer after the legendary MC Mary Kom to win the continental gold.“I wanted to quit boxing. But I continued. I had to change the colour of my medal. It was very important. More important than that is that I continued,” Lovlina said after defeating China's Ziyi Bao 5-0 in the women's 75kg final.Lovlina had won an Olympic bronze at Tokyo 2020 but returned from Paris without a medal. She subsequently took a year-long break before making her return to international boxing.The comeback, however, was far from smooth. She exited the World Championships in the second round and later skipped the World Boxing Cup final. At the Commonwealth Games this year, she had to settle for silver — a result that left her dissatisfied.“It was a tough year for me,” she said. “I was not happy about winning the silver medal at the Commonwealth Games. But, there are a lot of things in an athlete's life: losses, injuries. You have to handle a lot of things. This gold medal was very important to me.”The gold in Japan completed a remarkable turnaround for the boxer from Assam, who had won silver at the previous Asian Games after losing to China's Li Qian.Lovlina held her nerve in a closely fought final against Bao. She edged the opening round 3-2 on the judges' scorecards before winning the second 4-1. She maintained her composure in the final round to secure another 4-1 verdict and complete a 5-0 victory.The triumph ended India's 12-year wait for a women's Asian Games boxing champion, with Mary Kom having won flyweight gold at the 2014 edition in Incheon.Lovlina, however, was still taking in the magnitude of her achievement.“That is how I continued. I am feeling good. I don't know how to celebrate my gold. It has just ended. I need some time to accept that I have won. I am feeling very good.”Lovlina said the journey had also been about overcoming self-doubt. Looking back at her younger self, she said she would remind herself of the ability she possessed.“I had no confidence at that time, so if I had the chance to talk to my younger self I would tell her, 'You are confident, you are the best'. Now, I have a medal in every competition.”Mental strength, she added, was crucial when facing high-quality opponents.“I think it is important to be mentally strong. If we think that we have to win, no one can defeat us.”Japan, meanwhile, has now delivered another major moment in Lovlina's career.“I have to be strong and win. I was very positive about everything. Japan is very lucky for me. I was always think about winning.”And when asked whom she would call first after winning the biggest title of her Asian Games career, there was little hesitation.“The first person I am going to call is my mum. She doesn't watch my matches because she's very worried,” she said.
Article Summary: Lovlina borgohain won asian games gold on her 29th birthday. She defeated china's ziyi bao 5-0 in the women's 75kg final. The 29-year-old had contemplated walking away from boxing after returning empty-handed from the paris olympics.
